title: Environment-aware rollout engine for canaries, A/B, and shadow traffic
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement an environment-aware rollout engine that interprets a single rollout policy into concrete actions for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The engine must support canary rollouts, weighted A/B experiments, shadow traffic forwarding, and auto-rollback triggers while respecting environment-specific constraints (network egress, KMS access, RBAC, offline upgrades). The goal is consistent developer ergonomics (one policy language) with predictable behavior across environments and built-in safeguards for privacy and availability.
acceptance_criteria: Single rollout policy language defined and documented in Confluence (policy grammar + examples for canary, A/B, shadow)
Policy translator implemented that outputs environment-specific plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private
Canary rollouts support staged percentages (0,1,5,10,25,50,100) with time-based and metric-based progression for all environments
Shadow traffic implementation forwards replica requests with tagging and isolated billing in Hosted and Dedicated; in Private, shadow forwards are optional and subject to customer ACLs
Auto-rollback rules that combine SLO breach detection (latency/error rate) with quality regressions (eval prompt set delta) and trigger safe fallback within configured windows
End-to-end integration tests covering policy translation and simulated rollouts in the testbed cluster for each environment
Docs and Console UX mocks for policy authoring, rollout monitoring, and manual override controls
tasks: Write policy grammar RFC and examples (Confluence) - owner: Asha
Implement policy translator service - owner: Marco
Add environment adapters: hosted-adapter, dedicated-adapter, private-adapter - owner: infra team
Expose rollout controls in Console (UI/UX) and API endpoints - owner: product-dev
Implement shadow forwarding with non-blocking telemetry and billing tags - owner: runtime team
Define auto-rollback heuristics and integrate with SLO engine and evals pipeline - owner: reliability
Create synthetic canary runner and integration tests in testbed - owner: qa
Security review and Private deployment checklist (KMS, no egress) - owner: security
Docs: Quickstart, examples for A/B, canary, shadow, and failure-mode playbook - owner: docs
notes: Trade-offs: single policy language reduces cognitive load but requires robust translator and clear lints to surface unsupported constructs per environment
Hosted constraints: full access to telemetry, shadowing allowed without additional ACLs; we can run aggressive auto-rollback based on near-real-time metrics
Dedicated constraints: customers may enable limited shadowing; autoscaling interactions must be considered to avoid over-provisioning during ramp

Private constraints: often air-gapped or strict egress rules. Policy translator must emit an operator plan (manifest) rather than attempting remote hooks; shadowing may be disabled by default and require explicit customer opt-in

Auto-rollback signals: combine infra SLOs (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate), feature-quality deltas from evals (BLEU/ROUGE-like or domain-specific metrics), and human override windows. Default strategy: conservative — require 2 consecutive windows of breach before rollback unless customer config is aggressive
Instrumentation: all rollout traffic must carry rollout_id and cohort metadata; shadow traffic must include 'shadow=true' header and be tagged in cost reports
Cost control: limit max shadow RPS per customer in Dedicated/Private to avoid surprise charges; surface projected cost in Console before enabling shadow
RBAC: only users with 'deploy.can_rollout' can create policies that perform live traffic splitting; Private operator role must approve policy manifests
Migration: existing rollout/traffic-splitting rules must be importable via a one-time compatibility script
Edge cases: model variant incompatibility (different tokenizer/sequence length) must be validated during translation and either rejected or have graceful fallback instructions
